page.body:
## MemoryOS-owned checklist group 4 Step 1

The authoritative project record describes **Local AI phone comparison — checklist group 4 Step 1** as completed engineering and evaluation work on the owner-selected iOS Simulator—not as a phone-availability-gated activity. C39–C40 changed the status from an unfinished phone prerequisite to a completed real local-AI evaluation. See the [task record](docs/tasks/2026-11-14-local-ai-phone-evaluation.md), [resume summary](docs/evidence/local-ai-2026-11-14/resume-summary.md), [development-memory correction](docs/evidence/local-ai-2026-11-14/development-memory-correction.md), and [current README](README.md).

## What MemoryOS owns and what was completed

The completed scope is the MemoryOS-owned evaluation path: an isolated native lab, an independent evaluation core, replaceable integrations/adapters, app-owned original records, pinned/reviewed assets, and measured-result gates. The original records remain owned by the app rather than by an external runtime or provider. The evaluation compares the requested local candidates—Wax, a supported Cactus-based memory configuration, llama.cpp, Qwen3-1.7B, and other suitable local candidates—against the same fictional multilingual cases. This summary is limited to the app/configuration/process/evaluation results, not general vendor implementation. (Evidence: [task record](docs/tasks/2026-11-14-local-ai-phone-evaluation.md); [resume summary](docs/evidence/local-ai-2026-11-14/resume-summary.md).)

## Evidence and source identity

The retained evidence consists of **31 selected reports**, covering **450 completed Simulator operations** and **15 explicitly recorded MLX-unavailable cases**. The checks were actual, separate **SDK**, **canonical**, and **offline** checks, with separate Mac MLX execution. Simulator results are identified as Simulator results; they must not be presented as physical-phone measurements. The evidence preserves the original six evaluation outcomes and app-owned records. (Evidence: [resume summary](docs/evidence/local-ai-2026-11-14/resume-summary.md); [development-memory correction](docs/evidence/local-ai-2026-11-14/development-memory-correction.md).)

## Evaluation result versus adoption status

The engineering path is complete even though the quality gate failed for production adoption. Arabic, Iraqi, and source-quality results were insufficient, so no production model was adopted. The recorded recommendation is limited to **llama.cpp CPU** and **Wax lexical** as experimental baselines. This does not make the completed native lab, core, adapters, or evaluation partial; it means the measured result did not authorize production use. (Evidence: [resume summary](docs/evidence/local-ai-2026-11-14/resume-summary.md); [current README](README.md).)

## Boundaries and authorization

Step 1 does not authorize a later stage. Independent Step 2, physical-device readiness, and Step 3 remain separate from this completed Simulator evaluation. Physical latency, memory, storage, battery, and thermal measurements—and final physical-device component selection—remain unresolved; no physical battery or heat claim may be inferred from Simulator work. The retrieved project record also states that cloud transfer, release, and production selection are outside this work. (Evidence: [task record](docs/tasks/2026-11-14-local-ai-phone-evaluation.md); [resume summary](docs/evidence/local-ai-2026-11-14/resume-summary.md).)

## Historical work kept separate

The five-layout design-review prototype and the stopped-download/resume directive are historical, separate work. They must not be used to downgrade or redefine the completed C40 Simulator Step 1 evaluation. The five-layout initiative was design exploration rather than native application delivery, while the download instruction was a planned directive—not a verified implementation result. (Evidence: [development-memory correction](docs/evidence/local-ai-2026-11-14/development-memory-correction.md); [current README](README.md).)

## Implementation status in one sentence

**Completed:** MemoryOS-owned native lab/core/adapters and reproducible Simulator evaluation, with canonical/offline/SDK evidence and source-identified reports. **Failed or unresolved:** production-quality adoption and physical-device readiness. **Not authorized by Step 1:** any later stage, cloud use, or release.
